entry: Plateau in Central, South and East Asia. It is the world's largest and highest plateau, with an area of 2,500,000 square kilometers (970,000 sq mi) and an average elevation exceeding 4,500 meters (14,800 ft). It is surrounded by mountain ranges including the [[Himalayas]], and contains the world's two highest summits, [[Mount Everest]] and [[K2]]. Most of the [[Tibet Autonomous Region]] lies on the plateau, as do most of Qinghai and the western half of [[Sichuan]]. The plateau holds the headwaters of most streams in the surrounding regions, including the Yellow, [[Yangtze]] and [[Mekong]] rivers. Its glaciers act as a natural "water tower," and its ice fields hold the largest reserve of fresh water outside the polar regions. The impact of [[Climate change|climate change]] on the plateau is of ongoing scientific interest.

East Asian ethnic group native to Tibet. The 2020 census counted 7,060,700 Tibetans in China, including 3,137,900 in the [[Tibet Autonomous Region]]. Significant communities also live in the Chinese provinces of Gansu, Qinghai, [[Sichuan]] and [[Yunnan]], and in India, Nepal and Bhutan, with further communities in the [[United States]]. The Tibetic languages form a branch of the Tibeto-Burman language family. Most Tibetans practice [[Buddhism|Tibetan Buddhism]], although a significant minority follow the Indigenous Bon religion, and small communities of Muslims and Christians also exist. Tibetan Buddhism shapes Tibetan art, drama and architecture, while the region's harsh geography has produced an adaptive culture of Tibetan medicine and cuisine.

Paper-and-pencil game for two players, called noughts and crosses in Commonwealth English. Players alternately mark the nine spaces of a three-by-three grid with Xs and Os, and the first to complete a row, column or diagonal wins. With best play from both sides the game always ends in a draw, making it a solved game. Because of its simplicity, it is often used to teach good sportsmanship and game-tree search in [[Artificial intelligence|artificial intelligence]]. The first computerized version was developed in 1952 on the EDSAC computer at the [[University of Cambridge]].

Parasitic [[Arachnid|arachnid]] of the order Ixodida, part of the mite superorder Parasitiformes. Adult ticks are about 3 to 5 mm long but grow larger when engorged with blood, and have eight legs. Ticks feed on the blood of mammals, birds, and sometimes reptiles and amphibians, and are widely distributed, especially in warm, humid climates. Hard ticks (Ixodidae) have a hard dorsal shield, the scutum, while soft ticks (Argasidae) do not. Ticks pass through four life stages: egg, [[Larva|larva]], [[Nymph (biology)|nymph]] and adult. As disease vectors they transmit many serious illnesses to humans and other animals, including [[Lyme disease]]. The oldest known tick fossils are about 100 million years old, from the [[Cretaceous]] period. The most primitive living lineage is *Nuttalliella namaqua*, found in southern Africa from Tanzania to Namibia and South Africa.

Gravitational state in which a body's rotation period matches its orbital period around a larger partner. Tidal locking occurs when gravitational interaction slows a body's [[Rotation|rotation]] until its rotation rate no longer changes over a complete orbit. As a result, the [[Moon]] always shows the same face to [[Earth]]. Usually only the satellite is locked to the larger body, but where both masses and distances are relatively small, each can be locked to the other, as with [[Pluto]] and [[Charon (moon)|Charon]]. Friction from tidal bulges dissipates rotational energy as heat, and the process that ends in locking is called tidal despinning. Some sources use the term only for 1:1 synchronous rotation, while others include resonances such as that of [[Mercury (planet)|Mercury]], which completes three rotations for every two orbits of the [[Sun]].

Periodic rise and fall of sea level, caused mainly by the gravity of the [[Moon]] and the [[Sun]]. Tides result from differential gravitational forces combined with the orbital motion of the Earth–Moon system and the [[Earth's rotation|Earth's rotation]]. [[Isaac Newton]] described the gravitational cause mathematically in 1687. Most coasts have ocean tides that rise and fall about twice a day, though the shape of ocean basins, [[Coast|coastlines]] and friction modify their height and timing. Tidal range varies over a two-week cycle: near [[Full moon|full]] and new moons, when the Sun and Moon align, spring tides produce higher high waters and lower low waters, while at quarter moons neap tides are milder. Storm surges caused by [[Wind|wind]] and barometric pressure can also change sea level, especially in shallow seas and near coasts.

Archipelago off the southern tip of South America, across the [[Strait of Magellan]]. Its main island, Isla Grande de Tierra del Fuego, covers 73,746 sq km (28,473 sq mi). The western part, about two-thirds of the archipelago, belongs to [[Chile]], and the eastern part to Argentina. Its southernmost point, [[Cape Horn]], lies just north of 56° south. [[Ferdinand Magellan]] named the islands during his 1520 expedition, after the fires built by the Indigenous inhabitants. The earliest-known human settlement dates to c. 8,000 BC. European settlement began in the second half of the 19th century, during a Patagonian [[Sheep|sheep]] farming boom and a gold rush, and displaced native populations. Today [[Petroleum|petroleum]] extraction dominates the economy of the north, while tourism, manufacturing and Antarctic logistics are important in the south.

Large cat of the genus *Panthera* native to Asia. The tiger (*Panthera tigris*) is the largest living member of the [[Felidae|cat family]], with a powerful, muscular body and orange fur marked with black, mostly vertical stripes. It inhabits mainly forests, from coniferous and temperate broadleaf forests in the Russian Far East and northeastern China to tropical forests in India and Southeast Asia. An [[Apex predator|apex predator]], it hunts mainly [[Ungulate|hooved mammals]] by ambush and lives a mostly solitary life. Females usually bear two or three cubs. Since the early 20th century tigers have lost at least 93% of their historic range, and the IUCN lists the species as Endangered. Major threats include [[Deforestation|deforestation]] and poaching for fur and for body parts used in traditional medicine. Tigers have featured prominently in the [[Folklore|folklore]] of cultures across their range.

American professional golfer. Woods turned professional in 1996 and won the 1997 Masters by a record 12 strokes. His 15-stroke victory at the 2000 U.S. Open is regarded by many as the greatest performance in golf history. Winning the 2001 Masters completed four consecutive major championships, a feat known as the "Tiger Slam." He was world number one for 264 consecutive weeks from 1999 to 2004 and for 281 consecutive weeks from 2005 to 2010. He has won 15 major championships, second only to [[Jack Nicklaus]]'s 18, and 82 PGA Tour events, tied with Sam Snead. After four back surgeries between 2014 and 2017, he won the 2019 Masters, his first major in 11 years. A 2021 single-car collision caused serious leg injuries, and he returned to the PGA Tour in 2022. In 2026 he was involved in another car crash and reached a plea deal for willful reckless driving.

Large ground shark, the only living member of the genus *Galeocerdo*. Females can exceed 5 m (16 ft 5 in), and the largest males reach about 4 m. Its dark stripes, which fade with age, resemble a tiger's pattern. The solitary, mostly nocturnal tiger shark has the widest food spectrum of any shark, eating [[Crustacean|crustaceans]], fish, [[Sea turtle|sea turtles]], [[Squid|squid]], [[Dolphin|dolphins]] and smaller sharks. It is known as a "garbage eater" because it swallows inedible objects, and its only recorded natural predator is the [[Orca|orca]]. The species is second only to the [[Great white shark|great white]] in recorded fatal attacks on humans, though these remain rare. Finning and fishing have led to a Near Threatened listing on the IUCN Red List.

King of Armenia, of the Artaxiad dynasty, reigning from 95 to 55 BC. Under Tigranes the [[Armenia|Armenian]] kingdom expanded beyond its traditional boundaries and reached its peak, and he took the title King of Kings. At its height his empire stretched from the Pontic Alps to Mesopotamia and from the [[Caspian Sea]] to the Mediterranean, and captured vassals extended it to the [[Red Sea]] and the Persian Gulf. He moved inhabitants of conquered cities to his new capital, Tigranocerta, and invited Greek rhetoricians and philosophers to his court. He married the daughter of [[Mithridates VI Eupator]] of Pontus, and later sheltered Mithridates after his defeats by Rome. Roman forces under Lucullus defeated him at Tigranocerta in 69 BC and at Artaxata a year later. In 66 BC [[Pompey]] invaded; Tigranes surrendered, kept the heartland of his kingdom as a Roman buffer state, and lost his conquests.

Armed conflict in Ethiopia, 2020–2022. Fought mainly in Tigray from 3 November 2020, it pitted Ethiopian federal forces, allied with [[Eritrea]], against the Tigray People's Liberation Front. Federal forces captured Mekelle on 28 November, but Tigrayan forces retook it in June 2021. A humanitarian truce in March 2022 gave way to renewed fighting in late August. A cessation of hostilities agreed on 2 November 2022 excluded Eritrea, which continued to occupy parts of Tigray. All sides committed [[War crime|war crimes]], and Ethiopian and Eritrean forces were accused of [[Genocide|genocide]]. Between 100,000 and 600,000 people were killed. Fighting resumed in 2026.

River in [[Turkey]], [[Syria]] and [[Iraq]], the eastern of the two rivers that define [[Mesopotamia]]. It rises in the Taurus Mountains of eastern Turkey and flows about 1,750 km (1,090 mi) south, passing [[Baghdad]], Mosul, Tikrit and Samarra. It merges with the [[Euphrates]] to form the Shatt al-Arab before reaching the [[Persian Gulf]]. In ancient times the river nurtured the Assyrian Empire, and cities such as [[Nineveh]] and Ctesiphon stood on its banks. The Mandaeans still use it for baptism. Shallow-draft vessels can reach Baghdad, and the river is heavily dammed in Iraq and Turkey for irrigation and flood control. Modern threats include geopolitical instability, dam projects, poor water management and climate change.

City (pop., 2024: 2,297,000) in northwestern Mexico, the largest in [[Baja California]]. It is the seat of Tijuana Municipality and lies on the Mexico–United States border, forming with [[San Diego]] the largest bi-national conurbation shared by the [[United States]] and Mexico. The city was incorporated on 11 July 1889. It is a major manufacturing center for North America, hosting many multinational [[Conglomerate (company)|conglomerate]] companies, and in the early 21st century it emerged as the medical device manufacturing capital of North America. It is the most visited border city in the world, with more than fifty million people crossing between it and San Diego each year. Violent crime linked to organized crime and cartels is high, and the city regularly ranks among the most violent by homicide rate.

Chinese short-form video [[Social networking service|social networking service]]. Users post videos from three seconds to 60 minutes long through a [[Mobile app|mobile app]] or website. Its parent company, the Beijing-based ByteDance, launched the Chinese app Douyin in 2016 and TikTok internationally in September 2017. Its recommendation algorithm connects creators with new audiences, and the app passed two billion mobile downloads in April 2020. TikTok is blocked in mainland [[China]] and [[Hong Kong]], where Douyin is available instead, and a minority of countries, including [[India]] and [[Afghanistan]], have full or partial bans. In January 2026 a U.S. joint venture was formed to handle TikTok's American operations, with [[Oracle Corporation|Oracle]] and Silver Lake among the investors and ByteDance holding 19.9%. Critics have raised concerns about data privacy, mental health, misinformation and the company's ties to China.

Ruined ancient [[Maya civilization|Maya]] city in the Petén Department of northern Guatemala. Tikal, likely called Yax Mutal in antiquity, was one of the largest Maya urban centers and the capital of one of its most powerful kingdoms. Monumental architecture dates to the 4th century BC, but the city peaked in the Classic Period (c. 200 to 900). It dominated much of the Maya region and interacted with [[Teotihuacan]] in the Valley of Mexico, and a ruling dynasty was founded by conquerors from Teotihuacan in the 4th century AD. Its long dynastic ruler list has helped archaeologists locate many royal tombs. The city was abandoned by the end of the 10th century after elite palaces were burned and the population declined. The mapped site covers more than 16 square km and includes about 3,000 structures on [[Limestone|limestone]] ridges. It has been a UNESCO World Heritage Site since 1979.

Common name for many species of [[Cichlid|cichlid]] fish. Tilapia are mainly freshwater fish native to Africa and the Middle East, found in shallow streams, ponds, rivers and lakes, and less often in brackish water. They are important in artisanal fishing in Africa and in [[Aquaculture|aquaculture]]. Tilapia are mouth-brooders that carry their eggs and young in the mouth for several days. They can become an [[Invasive species|invasive]] species in warm habitats such as Australia, but generally not in temperate climates, where they cannot survive cold water. Traditionally an affordable food in the Philippines, tilapia has been the fourth-most consumed fish in the United States since 2002. In [[Ancient Egypt|ancient Egypt]] the fish symbolized rebirth and was associated with [[Hathor]], goddess of fertility. Some Nile tilapia grow to 60 cm (2 ft).

Scottish actress. Swinton began her career in Derek Jarman's experimental films and won the Volpi Cup for Best Actress for her role as Isabella of France in *Edward II* (1991). She received the Academy Award for Best Supporting Actress for *Michael Clayton* (2007). She played the Ancient One in the [[Marvel Cinematic Universe]] (2016–2019) and the White Witch in *The Chronicles of Narnia* films. She frequently works with [[Wes Anderson]], including in *Moonrise Kingdom* and *The Grand Budapest Hotel*. In 2020 [[The New York Times]] ranked her among the greatest actors of the 21st century.

Genus of about 30 species of mostly large deciduous trees, native to the temperate Northern Hemisphere. Known as lime or linden in Europe and Asia and as basswood in North America, it has its greatest species diversity in Asia. Many species hybridize readily, so the exact species count is uncertain. The heart-shaped leaves bear strongly scented yellow flowers that attract bees, and the white wood is soft and fine-grained, popular for carving. The genus was once placed in the family Tiliaceae but is now included in [[Malvaceae]]. It is the only known ectomycorrhizal genus in that family.

Agricultural preparation of [[Soil|soil]] by mechanical agitation, such as digging, stirring and overturning. Tillage can be done by hand with tools such as [[Hoe (tool)|hoes]] and shovels, or by draft animals and machines pulling [[Plough|plows]] and [[Harrow (tool)|harrows]]. Primary tillage, such as plowing, loosens the soil and mixes in fertilizer or plant material, leaving a rough surface. Secondary tillage produces finer soil, shapes the seedbed and controls weeds, which are uprooted or buried. Plows have been pulled by people, [[Ox|oxen]], mules and water buffalo, and the earliest evidence of plow use dates to around 4000 BCE in Mesopotamia. Mechanized [[Tractor|tractors]] enabled deeper soil inversion, but excessive plowing of native grasslands contributed to the [[Dust Bowl]] of the 1930s in the United States. Conservation tillage, which disturbs less of the soil surface and keeps crop residue, covered about 72% of U.S. cropland in 2017, helping to reduce [[Erosion|erosion]].

American actor and comedian. Known for playing Tim "The Toolman" Taylor on the ABC [[Sitcom|sitcom]] *Home Improvement* (1991–1999), for which he won a Golden Globe Award. He voices Buzz Lightyear in the [[Toy Story]] franchise and played [[Santa Claus]] in the *Santa Clause* films. He starred as Mike Baxter in the sitcom *Last Man Standing* (2011–2021). His other films include *Galaxy Quest* (1999) and *Wild Hogs* (2007). After a 1978 cocaine conviction, he served prison time and returned to comedy after his release in 1981.

English computer scientist, inventor of the [[World Wide Web]]. On 12 March 1989 he proposed an information-management system at [[CERN]], the European Organization for Nuclear Research. He devised and implemented the first web browser and web server, and invented [[HTML]], [[HTTP]] and the [[URL]] system. He founded the World Wide Web Consortium (W3C), which oversees the Web's continued development. He is a professorial research fellow at the [[University of Oxford]] and professor emeritus at the [[Massachusetts Institute of Technology]]. He was knighted by [[Elizabeth II|Queen Elizabeth II]] in 2004 and received the 2016 Turing Award for inventing the Web, the first web browser and the fundamental protocols that let the Web scale.

American filmmaker and animator. Known for pioneering the [[Goth subculture|Goth]] style in Hollywood, he blends Gothic horror and dark fantasy with whimsical and surreal elements. His films include *Batman* (1989), *Edward Scissorhands* (1990), *Big Fish* (2003) and *Sweeney Todd: The Demon Barber of Fleet Street* (2007). He produced *The Nightmare Before Christmas* (1993), based on a poem he wrote. Composer [[Danny Elfman]] has scored all but three of his films. He directed several episodes of the [[Netflix]] series *Wednesday*. He has won one Emmy Award and received nominations for two [[Academy Awards|Academy Awards]].

American business executive. Cook was [[Chief executive officer|chief executive]] of [[Apple Inc.|Apple]] from 2011 until 2026, when John Ternus succeeded him as CEO and Cook became executive chairman. He joined Apple in 1998 as senior vice president for worldwide operations and served as chief operating officer under [[Steve Jobs]] before becoming chief executive. Under Cook, Apple's market value rose from $348 billion in 2011 to more than $4 trillion in 2026, and the company introduced products including AirPods, Apple Watch and Apple Vision Pro. In 2014 he became the first chief executive of a Fortune 500 company to publicly come out as gay.

American former basketball player and coach. Duncan spent his entire 19-season career with the [[San Antonio]] Spurs of the [[National Basketball Association]]. A native of Saint Croix in the U.S. Virgin Islands, he was the first overall pick in the 1997 NBA draft and was named Rookie of the Year. He won five NBA championships, three Finals MVP awards and two MVP awards. Nicknamed "the Big Fundamental," he is the only player selected to the All-NBA and All-Defensive teams for 13 consecutive seasons. He was inducted into the Naismith Memorial Basketball Hall of Fame in 2020.
